Playbook.name: AD — Kerberoasting: RC4 Service Ticket Requested - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access / Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A service ticket (4769) was requested with RC4 encryption (0x17) for a service account - RC4 tickets are the offline-crackable material Kerberoasting harvests. Triage question: is the REQUESTING principal sweeping many SPNs, or is this a legacy RC4-only service doing business as usual?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Cracked service-account passwords in a bank frequently carry high privilege (DB engines, middleware) and rarely rotate - one cracked SPN can be domain-wide impact.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: RC4 service ticket
Signal.Details: 4769 TicketEncryptionType 0x17; krbtgt and known-noise SPN rpap excluded by the rule.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Sweep = many distinct SPNs from one requestor in minutes: treat as active Kerberoasting.
Single SPN + legacy RC4-only service + fixed source: verify legacy status before closing.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether $username/$source_ip harvested crackable service tickets (sweep) or a legacy RC4 dependency fired the rule.

Step.name: Requestor SPN breadth in the last hour
Step.Purpose: Kerberoasting tools request many SPNs quickly; business clients request the handful they use.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4769" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | STATS req = COUNT(*), spns = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.ServiceName), enc_types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType), services = VALUES(winlog.event_data.ServiceName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: spns >= 5 in an hour with RC4 = sweep. spns 1-2 = normal usage or a single-target roast (check INV-02).

Step.name: Who else requested this SPN with RC4 today
Step.Purpose: If ONLY legacy clients ever request this SPN in RC4, the account is RC4-limited (misconfig). If a new requestor appeared, that requestor is the suspect.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4769" AND winlog.event_data.ServiceName == "$service" AND winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType == "0x17" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS req = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, src | SORT req DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A stable small set of requestors = the service's normal clients negotiating RC4 (account lacks AES keys). A one-off new requestor = roast attempt against this SPN.

Step.name: Requestor's own session origin
Step.Purpose: Roasts are run from a foothold - identify where the requesting account is logged on from.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Requestor active on an unusual workstation/server for that user, or via network logon from a non-standard host, raises suspicion of a compromised session being used to roast.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the requestor pulling RC4 tickets for 5+ distinct SPNs within the hour.
Node.Result: True Positive (Kerberoasting Sweep - escalate, reset exposed service accounts)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows a NEW requestor for this SPN while its historical RC4 clients are a fixed legacy set.
INV-02 shows only the same stable legacy clients requesting this SPN in RC4 (service account has no AES keys).
Requestor is a vulnerability scanner or audit tool with a documented schedule.
Breadth is 2-4 SPNs with no clear legacy explanation and requestor origin is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-ROAST-BREADTH, INV-02-ROAST-SPN, INV-03-ROAST-ORIGIN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Approved assessment tooling enumerating SPN tickets on schedule.

Indicators.Item: Requestor is the documented scanner account/host (e.g. Nessus service).

SOCAction.Item: Verify with vulnerability management; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Harvesting of crackable RC4 service tickets - single target or sweep.

Indicators.Item: Many SPNs from one requestor in minutes.
New requestor for an SPN with an otherwise stable client set.
Requestor session originates from an unusual host.

SOCAction.Item: Reset passwords of all SPN accounts requested (long/random or gMSA).

Misconfiguration.Definition: A service account limited to RC4 (no AES keys / msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes not set) makes every normal client request look roast-like.

Indicators.Item: Same legacy client set requesting for months.
Account created long ago; password predates AES.

SOCAction.Item: Rotate the service-account password to (re)generate AES keys and set supported-encryption-types.
Re-test; alerts for that SPN should disappear.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the requestor's live session and owner.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reset exposed SPN account passwords; prefer gMSA migration.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Eliminate RC4-only service accounts (rotate passwords to mint AES keys).
Alert on new SPN additions (companion rule PB-AD-012).

QualityChecks.Check: Rule already excludes krbtgt and the rpap noise SPN - verify rpap is still expected.
Cracking is offline; absence of immediate misuse does not clear a sweep.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Legacy RC4 client set documented; remediation plan for AES recorded.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: All requested SPN accounts rotated; roasting host contained and examined.
